chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, from their father, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

A man died and bequeathed to me and to another, or to two men (as executors). So one of them said, 'Take half of what he left and give me the half from what he left.' So the other refused him. They asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, so he said: 'That is for him (that he should refuse to take the half but they both should act as per the original bequest)'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one of two appointed executors tries to take half the estate for himself?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the refusal of one executor to accept a unilateral claim of half the estate, emphasizing that executors act as trustees bound by the testator's specific instructions rather than personal entitlement. This highlights the Shia legal principle of *amanah* (trusteeship), where fiduciary duty supersedes individual gain, ensuring the estate is distributed according to the deceased's will. The ruling underscores the importance of mutual consent and adherence to the original bequest structure in Islamic inheritance law.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from both his brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, from the father of them both, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said,

‘A man died and bequeathed to me and to another, or two men (to be executors). So one of the two said, ‘You take half of what has been left (legacy) and give me the (other) half from what has been left (legacy). So the other one refused him. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is for him (that he should refuse to take the half but they both should act as per the original bequest)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan from his two brothers, Muhammad and Ahmad from their father from Dawud ibn abu Yazid from Burayd ibn Mu’awiyah who has narrated the following:

“A man died and appointed me and another man or two men as executors for his will. One of them said, ‘I will deal with one-half of the legacy but the other one opposed, and they asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is for him (to disagree).”’
